reviews.text: Excellent care provided at their out of hours service. Very sensitive and responsive to my dog's needs.
Lovely friendly staff. Plenty of parking
I had to take a baby deer that someone had hit with their car but unfortunately it died from shock before it got some help. The staff couldn't do enough for me and helped in a very distressing time.

Prince was suffering from recurrent respiratory infections and frightening episodes affecting his breathing. I spent thousands of pounds trying to find out what was wrong with him, yet when expensive diagnostic tests were carried out, the results were not communicated to me. I repeatedly chased the practice for days, a booked telephone consultation never happened, and even after the matter was circulated to the wider veterinary team, nobody took responsibility. By the time Prince finally received doxycycline, approximately two weeks had passed.

Prince reacted terribly to the liquid medication. He cried, frothed, coughed and appeared to struggle to breathe. I immediately reported this and asked for tablets or an alternative formulation because I was frightened that he had inhaled the liquid. The vet refused and told me to continue giving it.

A more serious episode then followed. Prince began coughing, wheezing and struggling for breath as though he was having an asthma attack. I genuinely thought I was going to lose him. When I begged the practice for urgent help, I was spoken to in a hostile, patronising and demeaning manner and told that the vet was busy.

I was told I could not expect “special treatment” when all I was asking for was equal treatment, basic respect and urgent attention for a cat who could not breathe properly. It appeared that staff had already discussed me and decided that neither my concerns nor Prince’s condition would be treated fairly.

As his breathing deteriorated, I repeatedly asked for his medical records because another practice had agreed to see him as an emergency. Abbey House did not provide them in time, meaning I could not take him to the appointment I had arranged.

With no other option, I took Prince back to Abbey House and asked for him to be triaged immediately. Despite his breathing difficulties, he was left waiting while clients who arrived or booked later were taken through first. Several hours had passed since I first warned the practice that he was struggling to breathe, and one receptionist told me she was not bothered.

When Prince was eventually examined, the interaction was confrontational and distressing. He was handled in a way that increased his fear and appeared to worsen his breathing. I recorded part of the consultation because, by then, I no longer believed my account would be taken seriously.

His records were finally provided the following morning after another vets contacted them on my behalf and they had edited the notes. I have requested the full audit history and reported my concerns to the relevant veterinary body.

Prince was then examined elsewhere and diagnosed with pneumonia. I am now obtaining independent veterinary and legal advice to establish whether aspiration of the liquid medication, the instruction to continue it, the delay in urgent care and the refusal to release his records contributed to the pneumonia or caused permanent damage.

This was not one mistake. It was a chain of failures involving delayed results, missed calls, medication concerns, possible aspiration, difficulty obtaining emergency care, delayed medical records, hostile communication and what I believe was discriminatory treatment.

What happened could have had fatal consequences for Prince. I genuinely believe that the delay and refusal to help placed his life at risk.

The experience was horrific. I lost work, suffered severe anxiety and spent countless hours fighting for care and information while terrified that my cat might die. No pet owner should ever have to fight this hard for urgent veterinary treatment, medical records or basic respect.
Absolutely brilliant and great vet who listens and doesn't rush you. He saved my cats life
We were very happy with the service given.  The vets, nurses and receptionists are all very friendly and helpful. We wanted laparoscopic surgery and this veterinary hospital performs this procedure
My little lhaso apso puppy went for his first years health check and booster injection he went in happy, the vet was so gentle with him, I think he actually likes going 🐶👍
Happy place
They won’t see a pet unless they have its records from your usual vet’s - not helpful if it is out of hours and not providing the 24/7 emergency they claim they off

They put my cat down on Saturday. Had they referred me sooner maybe it might not have been needed. Got a call today (Thursday) saying it's not happened yet because I'd not paid. I didn't pay because I was waiting for the link they promised. Even in death they've mismanaged my poor cat. Extremely upsetting and unforgivable. I'd done plenty of grieving only to be distraught over this final interaction. Avoid these vets. £217 for euthanasia by the way. And I assume that's the cheapest option since I didn't want the ashes.

My mum took her dog here Rico and he had a bee sting and because they didn’t do there jobs my mum kept telling them it needs draining but they wouldn’t listen it turned into an abscess, it was really bad he had a massive hole in his neck they wasn’t helpful and over charged my mum and excused her of lying. Please don’t take your beloved pets here they do not care only money they care about.
Great service, the ease of getting an appointment the same day putting your mind at ease.
I felt confident with the place and the staff we saw
Really friendly staff and vet , really put us at ease while checking our cat over , hes now happily snoring away after treatment , thankyou ^^

We received amazing care whilst at Abbey House for an emergency appointment for our animal. We had an appointment straight away within the hour and although unfortunately our beloved pet didn’t come back with us, the vet we spoke to was incredibly supportive and thoughtful and explained things to us at our pace without rushing. The receptionist ladies were also incredibly kind and thoughtful and very down to earth. When we got our pet back, she was given to us in such a compassionate presentation. Our pets best interest was always at heart and we could not recommend them more. Thank you for looking after our Casper in her last moments♥️

Excellent communication
Excellent service 👍🏽

Generally a good vets but of late the wait times have gone up. On many occasions I have arrived early and have had to wait 15-20 minutes past my appointment time. This is fine as I can understand some pets need longer to diagnose and/or treat, or emergencies come in. I would happily wait 2 hours in such cases, and I have never complained. However this week I took my dog and got there 7 minutes late. Because of this I was told I would have to wait another 25 minutes before I would be seen, having been told I arrived late. Not happy on this occasion as I’m usually early and never complained if I’m not seen “7 minutes “ or more after my appointment time. It’s got to be a two way street here ABBEY HOUSE VETS. Please bear this in mind for future. Not happy this time.

I still reel today over my experiance with this company! I cant call them vets. No care for animals. I lost my Missy during covid. She had a tumor on her spleen. It had burst. Turned up . Was told to leave her in the doorway and stand back. Understood that with Covid. They turned. Up with a blanket. Put her in it and carried her like that between them both.  Missy jumped out to get to us. They just threw her back to there carriier blanket. They were just laughing and catching up on life?. Not concerned about my Missy!. Rang me to say she was not going to live. Asked them to bring her back  out so i could cuddle her while she passed. Told me they couldnt do it?.Just told me , i needed to pay 280 quid. No compassion. Whatsoever! They call themselves vets. Lol! . To my MissyX
When I arrived, the surgery was full of pets, which is a good sign. The practice is good otherwise it would be empty.
Very friendly staff, very clean and well maintained environment, very calming for all pets

I totally disappointed with this vets.  After being taken over by Croft house  vets and them closing,  this was our alternative.

My 20yr old cat was diagnosed with cancer.  Some kind of unusual cancer.

It took nearly 9 days to get to talk to a vet.  After ringing them! Eventually spoke on a Saturday.

I was assured nothing really to be done as I refused invasive tests.  Steroids  to be left as a prescription for him.

As urgent,  am sure youll agree.

This was Saturday morning.   By Tuesday we'd heard nothing.   Upon ringing  o was utterly lied too and told they'd tried ringing me sunday!

Considering im self employed.   My phone is always on.  I didn't question it.

Upon collecting the medication.   Receptionist came back to her computer several times because the medication hadn't been administered.

Even the Receptionist agreed they'd lied.

Nope.  You are not worthy of my pets lives and wellbeing.

0 stars.

My experience with Abbey House Vets

I am extremely disappointed with my recent experience at Abbey House Vets and have completely lost faith in the practice.

I dropped my dog off at 8am for an operation and spent the entire day feeling extremely worried. At around 1.30pm, I rang to check how she was doing, only to be told, to my horror, that she had not even been taken down to theatre yet. I find it unacceptable that I had to ring myself to find this out.

At around 4pm, I received a call to say that they had found another lump and wanted to make me aware of it and check whether it was an umbilical hernia. I explained that I was aware of it and had previously mentioned it. I had been told before that as long as my dog was happy, they were happy, so I was concerned that this was suddenly being raised on the day of her operation.

I was told that if it was an umbilical hernia, it would cost an additional £150, but if it was a fatty lump, there would be no extra charge. Naturally, I was concerned about this additional cost, but I wanted to do what was best for my dog.

I asked to be contacted once her operation was completed to let me know that she was okay. Unfortunately, I somehow missed the call and received a voicemail instead, telling me to collect her at 7.30pm.

When I arrived to collect her, I had to ask what had happened rather than being clearly informed. I was then told that it was indeed an umbilical hernia and an extra £150 had been added to my bill.

My poor dog was very drowsy and was drooling excessively when I brought her home, which caused me a great deal of concern. I was so worried that I spent the whole night with her and did not sleep.

What made the situation even worse was that three days later, I attended what was supposed to be a planned post-operative check-up. My dog was extremely nervous and shaking in the car, and I struggled to get her into the practice. After finally getting her upstairs, the receptionist was surprised to see me because there was no vet available that day. I was told that my appointment should have been cancelled. However, after checking, the appointment was still showing on the system and nobody had contacted me to cancel or rearrange it.

As a result, I have had no post-operative follow-up at all.

I feel that the communication and organisation throughout this entire experience were extremely poor. I had to chase information about my dog’s operation, I was given no proper explanation when collecting her unless I asked, and then I took my nervous and recovering dog to an appointment that should have been cancelled but nobody bothered to tell me about.

I have completely lost faith in this veterinary practice. I will not be returning, and I have cancelled my monthly plan because I no longer feel confident entrusting my dog to their care.

I am extremely disgruntled and disappointed with the way both my dog and I have been treated. As a paying customer and, most importantly, as a worried pet owner, I expected much better.

I’ve previously had to use abbey house due to poorly dogs and they’ve been absolute fantastic (this was two years ago)

On Wednesday night, my cat got admitted to hospital. The male vet we saw that evening for his admission was lovely and he spoke us through our cats treatment plan for 24 hours.

The issue came at 11am the next day when the female vet rang me and quoted me over the phone £1900 for an abdominal scan with sedation.
I told her I did not want him sedating due to bad previous experience and I would also like a price breakdown of everything because it’s a staggering amount of money, her response was ‘you won’t understand it’.

My partner has then gone to collect our cat because this just wasn’t acceptable. When he got there, the lovely girl on reception gave him a quote for his abdominal scan, sedation and full bloods - £650.

When he’s then gone into the room to speak to the vet, they discussed further treatment and said the best she could do was £630 just for the scan and sedation - my partner then proceeded to produce the estimated invoice and she left the room and he then had to speak to the nurse.

It is unprofessional, you’re taking advantage of pet parents in their most vulnerable state. Me and my partner spend that day having to have a conversation of where we drew the line on saving our 16 month old cat.

A conversation we DID NOT need to have because her pockets were too deep.

When I rang to check on at 8am, the nurse told me he was bright and comfortable. Why 3 hours later did the vet tell me she needed to give him calm tablets because he was uncomfortable?

My cat is now home, with antibiotics, he has eaten, he has urinated, he’s sleepy but he’s also had a lot of stress over 48 hours.

Your reception team, nurses and the male vet was fantastic. The female vet, nearly made us put our cat to sleep.

Amazing team who supported and cared for us during a very challenging experience
Thank you so much

My cat had a few medical procedures done during this visit. Absolutely lovely staff. Super kind to myself and welcoming to my cat. Love the separated waiting areas. Lovely vets! Thank you. Made my experience so much better
Always fantastic experience. Thank you

Seen promptly.
Good explanation of problem
Felt listened to and understood
Brilliant Vets, very professional service and welcoming throughout, thank you

First vet we saw (Jimmy) in an emergency for our dogs infection was very knowledgeable and helpful but after returning for the check up we encountered a useless vet who has to follow a procedure guide as she didn’t know how to treat our dogs infection. I believe she was called Jenny and the only thing she could tell me was I would need to spend £600 to have a sample of the infection sent off to a lab (despite the infection clearing and we just wanted more antibiotics to keep up with the process). We carried on with the antibiotics right to the end and the infection was nearly gone I rang in to get another weeks worth of antibiotics to be told this wouldn’t be an issue. The following day I rang back as I was told I’ll get a phone call when they were ready and I still hadn’t heard anything, only to find out the grossly incompetent vet has booked me an appointment at a date and time I can’t do and was never told about the day after making the call to reassess my dog and to try to squeeze more money. They did not care about my dogs health one bit only about the money they could make off of my dog.
Really bad experience, extremely poor communication whilst my cat was staying in there before he died. Wouldn’t recommend

I took my dachshund Dappie to abbey house vets in an emergency. What an amazing vets. Gave me totally confidence in what they were going to do with Daps. He had eaten toy fluff and became very ill. Having spent a couple of days with there fantastic team. He's now home and back to his self. I can't thank the team enough for what they have done. There truly lifesaver. Thank you all Colin.
Very efficient service.

Great vets overall but significantly reducing my star count for how ridiculously expensive they are. Also incredibly cheeky with the products they offer.. had it multiple times now that I’ve bought stuff at the vets and then searched for those same product online, just to find them for at least half the price! Same for if you ever need a AHC to travel with your pet to Europe. DO NOT GET THIS HERE. You can literally pay £100 or less elsewhere (Abby house does it for £200+).

First called up to register my cat. The online booking system is good but it requested a phone call for dental work. I called and they couldn't find evidence of my registration online. They told me they were too busy and they will call me back, but I never received a call. As I needed a consultation before dental work, I decided to use the online system to book a general appointment.

Upon arrival, the staff were very friendly and the place was nice and clean. However, they couldn't find my booking and actually had the wrong name for my pet down somehow. I showed the text I received evidencing I had registered the name correctly, plus I had had my previous vet forward the history to them, so unsure how this could have been keyed in wrongly.

The appointment was on time. After a 1-2 minute examination of my cat, I was told he could have a huge range of diseases and was quoted £620 for bloods and xray and a further possible £2k for tooth extraction for my cat It is worth adding he had been seen by a different vet 9 months prior who were confident that the cause was stomatitis and most of his teeth are already removed, so the quote is beyond extortionate if extraction is needed. Everywhere else can do all for an absolute max £1k for major dental work (confirmed directly by 2 very positively reviewed vets plus a google search will tell you the same).

Overall, really insulting prices quoted following a rushed check up. Profits clearly the big priority over care for animals.

I've been using Abbey House Morley for decades with my cats. I find all staff efficient,  competent and compassionate. The surgery is cat friendly when having to wait to be seen. No complaints at all.

Absouletly disgusted in this Vets Practice. I was with Abbey House for my cats for around 5 years. At the start there were no glaring issues; however as time has gone on, I have realised that this practice is only out for your money. There is no concern for the welfare of your animals and their vets are clearly inexperienced or resticted by policies which require them to tell lies to obtain the highest amount of money they can.

My cat was brought in having back to back seizures. They gave us two options 1. have an MRI and potenital brain surgery which would be 3-5 thousand pounds or 2. put him on medication for the rest of his life. There was no attempt to ascertain the cause of the seizures even though we were sure he had toxicity poisioning ( we have since learnt that a simple blood test would have confirmed this). We opted for the second offer as we could not afford 3-5k. We ended up bringing him back 3 times in one day because they kept telling us we could manage him at home despite him having 4 minute seizures back to back. Finally they agreed to monitor him overnight for an extremely large fee.

They are charging £50 for a medication that is £16 online. We paid £12 for a prescription. The prescription was written for the incorrect medication. They then wrote a further prescription which was rejected by the company selling the medication because it was not legally compliant. After finding out this, it took them over a week to rectify despite several phone calls and emails telling them that my cat needed this medication because he was epileptic and had run out. Due to their delay I had no option but to pay £50 for the medication from them on top of the £12 I had already paid for the prescription. If this isn't proof of them doing everything they can to obtain your money with no consideration for the welfare of the animal then I don't know what is!

They then told us our cat needed a blood test to check the medication levels in his system. Each time we brought him in we were told they were unable to take bloods because he was 'too difficult'. They told us to go home and give him sedatory medication so they could try it again. 3 separate visits and attempts it took them to take bloods. On the 3rd attempt the vet came out and said 'I think we might need to try numbing the area because he just won't let us put the needle in his neck'. Sorry but WHAT THE HELL were you doing trying to put a needle in a distressed cats neck WITHOUT attempting this with numbing cream. They managed to take the blood this time but said 'sorry we have caught his vein so he is bleeding a lot'. He had no hair on his neck and clear injuries from the needle. He literally looked traumatised. I only realised how bad all of this was when I took this 'very difficult' cat to an alternative vets and they took his bloods without issue in 5 minutes!!

To top it all off, I needed an urgent appointment for my cat who was having serious seizures again yesterday. After our past treatments and reading the reviews online, I opted for a new vet. The new vet requested his history from Abbey House, they told them he wasn't registered there! I rang up and they found him straight away and said they would send the documents over. Got to the appointment an hour later and they had sent nothing. The new vets have called expressing how urgent this is and I have emailed and still nothing. Once again, showing their absolute lack of concern for the welfare of the animal.

The above is only the half of what I have expeirenced at Abbey House but it is enough to put me off for good and should be enough to put any pet owner off bringing their beloved animals to this place.
Definitely expensive but good care
Amazing team of compassionate people who looked us and our beloved pet during a time of uncertainty and worry.  They do Amazing work and I cant thank them enough.

Worst experience in my life. BIG warning looks like my dogs are contagious with a dangerous virus and can pass to other dogs. I was at the clinic today between 16:30 till 17:20 and I’ve been in the waiting area where others dogs were on the scales where I saw other pets been, now I need to get a blood saole to make sure my dogs are not contagious. I think this is really bad and my wife afraid of taking the dog for a walk.   What is happening. Not good

****The worse vets I’ve ever had the misfortune of seeing*** Would not recommend unless you want to waste your money. Took my dog in as she was not looking well, she had a swollen neck and was yelping in pain on the odd occasion for no reason. After a 4hr wait we finally got to see the vet, the vet examined her neck said there was no concerns and gave us some pain relief and advised if it’s no better to go and see our registered vets. Now I am clearly not a vet but as part of a general wellness exam there are several things surely you would check.
1) if the symptoms in question are her neck I assume you would check in her mouth and down her throat to see if there are any issues there.
2) you would check her over everywhere to make sure there are not any other concerning factors.
Now the reason I say this as in the vets notes she wrote that she checked in her mouth and I can assure you as there was me and my partner in the room, she didn’t, so that’s a lie.
The next day we took her to our registered vet for a “consultation” they checked her over everywhere and within 5mins diagnosed her with an ulcer in her eye.
Now if your vet would have checked her over thoroughly they would have picked this up but they didn’t we paid over £200 for some pain relief medication.
We notified the vets of this and had a discussion with practice manager who basically said the ulcer might not of been there when we came in, I’m not sure how you would know if it’s there or not if you didn’t do a complete wellness check and I’m baffled how 6hrs later when we saw our registered vet the ulcer miraculously appeared! Oh by the way we also mentioned in our so called consultation she had gunk in her eye.
He then said regarding the vet checking in her mouth she has put in her notes she done this and you must of missed it??! I’m sorry, what! There was me and my partner in the room both of us never took our eyes of our dog so I’m not sure how we can miss this so I’ve now been called a liar.
In all honesty it’s not the money that I care about in the slightest, it’s the neglect shown to my dog, the lies, and if we would of taken there advice and just left her to see how she got on with the medication how much worse she would of got.
Your standards are minimal care and maximum profit, I would not take any of my animals to your vets and I would advise anyone to think very carefully before using these so called vets!
Very helpful and supportive when examining and vaccinating my feisty cat! Nice friendly staff

I took my dog as a precaution to been stung by bee on their advice, this was at 9pm, there was no swelling, no stinger to remove, but he had been a bit sick. She felt his back legs and his gums which took 2 mins. She charged me £205! Then she said it doesnt include the two jabs she gave him for £55. Basically £260 and I was in there 5 minutes and I come on no wiser than when I went in, im in disbelief that they can charge that amount for 5 minutes work and not be conclusive or put me to rest.
Excellent service
Excellent vets!

Absolutely shocking treatment!! We registered our pet Max after bringing him from Crete, with his pet passport. He can now be neutered and the vets told us we had to have a "telephone consultation" first. This was booked for 9am. Phone never rang (it get A LOT worse). I rang them and they eventually got a nurse to ring back. They said they didnt realise he was from crete and he had to have some bloods done or they won't castrate him saying max was "eastern european" Crete is not eastern European. Anyway they said we had to have the bloods done or no neutering. I went up to the vets that same day as my older dog was due his injections. Max had his the week before where we had to wait over 40 minutes (in the waiting area) just to be seen. I walk into the vets and the receptionist walked up and demanded I leave and sit in the car because Max needed testing for Brucella. I explained it wasn't an issue the week before but they still asked me to leave (oh it gets worse). Anyway the vet came to my car and said she had time to take Max's bloods that day as well as my other dogs injections. I agreed as we want him neutered. They then make me go through a back door (which was extremely traumatic as my two previous dogs had to be put down during covid and they refused to let me stay with them and forced me to leave them by the back door. I later found out from a parent on the school run who is also a vet nurse, that their practice allowed people to be with their pets, even in lockdown. Abbey house didnt care). Anyway, we get in there, the vet takes Max's bloods then my other dogs injections. ONLY THEN did the vet ask if we knew what the bloods were for and what the guidance is. I explained no one told us other than they were needed to castrate him. The vet then proceeded to tell me if the bloods were positive, then government guidelines are to put the dog down!!!!! I have never been so upset and disgusted in my life, had I had known, the bloods were not compulsory so I would not have had them done. Absolutely disgusting. I then got told to put my dogs back in the car to then pay. Absolutely awful practice. Only reason we are staying for now is because we have a pet plan where we may so much a month and that gets us 10% off neutering. We pay £20 per dog for this treatment. As soon as the neutering has been done we will look for another vets. Just DISGRACEFUL. To also find out during covid that other vets allowed you to be with your pets, even in lick down if they were being euthanised and Abbey house made me leave mine in the back porch, even when I begged them to do it in the porch or my car so I would be with them! I am a nurse so I was working all through covid any way. Unforgivable. We only stayed because our 3rd dog Oscar was registered with them and when we rang around some vets they said they were full. Someone at work said "even i know abbey house are a terrible vets and I dont have any pets
The staff were fantastic throughout, I was regularly updated about my dogs condition and he was looked after to a very high standard.
Would highly recommend, brilliant service, staff extremely helpful, the vet we saw was excellent she was very reassuring. Nurse was extremely helpful and excellent.
Not impressed first visit was good on my 2nd visit communication lacking then vet didn't have Wright equipment  couldn't find vine tried several times  ...then asked for 230 pounds
Very kind and we were kept informed at all stages.

This is an outstanding, values-based veterinary practice. Genuine friendliness of all the people I met. A very pleasant reception area with free coffee! Highly professional and empathetic vet who was extremely attentive, and explained clearly the reason for my dog’s symptoms. Very reasonably priced. I am so grateful for finding this practice. Thank you so much.

Disgusting! Avoid at all costs.
Booked my dog in to be put to sleep. Asked for the vet to see him and confirm I had come to the right decision. Had a 25 minute conversation with the receptionist. She asked if I wanted an extended appointment to which I said no as I don’t see why I would need to after she was well aware of my situation as we have been making this hard choice for months due to the elderly dogs quality of life.
Had the appointment booked two weeks in advance.
Arrived at the appointment time I asked for which was a Friday evening 6.30pm so none of us were up early for work on the Saturday morning.
Was told at 6.30 that only a consultation appointment was made for 15 mins as I declined an extended appointment.
I have no idea what the appointments are or for how long as I do not work in a vets.
We were then told we could wait till 7pm and they will be able to put him to sleep then. We all agreed clearly upset and crying to which we were told the cost would rise from £80 to £270 as it is “out of hours at 7pm”!!
Absolutely disgusting- they could have said as there was miscommunication the appointment could go ahead as there was no one else in there at that time but all they care about is the money.
I have used them for over 18 years and this is how you’re treated.
There is no care for the animals or the owners unless they are willing to pay disgusting amounts of money.
After calling another vet we have an appointment with them who also agree the treatment we received was outrageous.
I will never use them again and my other dogs will now be under a real caring vets.

I first took my cat to Abbey House at Morley in late September 2025, and it has taken me months to be able to write this feedback due to the emotional impact.
My cat was seen with a facial abscess. Although the abscess was assessed, it was not cleaned or flushed, and only basic checks were carried out (weight, temperature, lymph nodes). I explained that she was in pain, struggling to eat, and had developed a wobbly gait. The vet prescribed antibiotics in tablet form, and I had to repeat that she was struggling to eat before liquid Synulox was offered instead.
The vet then began typing up notes, and the consultation appeared to be over. I had to ask again about pain relief before being handed a quarter‑full bottle of Gabapentin, with no explanation of how to administer it. When I repeated my concern about her wobbly gait, I was told it was “arthritis,” despite no diagnostic tests being carried out. I was left confused about how such a conclusion had been reached.
No investigation into the root cause of the abscess was suggested. Her mouth and teeth were not examined, and no X‑ray, bloodwork, or imaging was recommended. There was also no discussion of home care or any follow‑up plan. Communication throughout was poor, and I felt I had to repeat the same symptoms multiple times just to be acknowledged.
Over the next few days, my cat deteriorated rapidly. She struggled to eat, drink and eventually could barely walk. I returned to the practice and saw a different vet, who suggested a CT scan, but by then, in our opinion, she was too weak and we didn’t want her to suffer further. This decision was not about the cost.
In hindsight, I wish I had taken her elsewhere after the first consultation. I believed I was paying for a professional assessment, but the service we received fell far short of that looking back.
Afterwards, I tried to raise my concerns with a senior staff member. I had to call numerous times over several days, speaking to five different people, only to discover my messages were not being passed on. I eventually escalated the issue to the practice manager, who apologised and acknowledged this was unacceptable. Unfortunately, the complaints process itself added to the distress, the process advertised on the website does not reflect my experience.
I then contacted the VCMS for mediation after Abbey House failed to address my concerns. The VCMS were helpful, but their powers are limited and rely on voluntary engagement from the practice.
Abbey House ultimately offered a 50% refund as a “goodwill gesture.” I declined, as I found this response insulting and not reflective of the issues raised.
I wish I had read all the reviews online, not only on the official Abbey House website, but also independent reviews such as Trust Pilot.
I have tried to keep personal emotion out of this review as much as possible, so readers can form their own opinion. It is my view that I paid a significant amount of money for my cat to be properly assessed and treated, and the standard of care she received was unacceptable. I have struggled to accept what happened and feel guilty about how she suffered following that initial consultation.
I hope nobody else has to experience what we endured.
Good friendly place. Also emergency hospital vets for Leeds

Emergency out of hours appointment after our Dog pinched a grape.
Straight in for an injection to make him sick. Happily he brought it up straight away.

I can’t thank the team at Abbey House enough for their compassion today. I brought in a rescue Mallard duck, and although the news was sad—she had to be put to sleep due to a severe prolapse—the staff handled the situation with such kindness and sensitivity. No explanation given by reception staff upon arrival
No consideration of alternative waiting arrangements

I was out of my area and had to rush my dog to the nearest emergency vet after she had managed to impale herself on a stick. She was initially inspected by a male vet immediately to ensure she was not at immediate risk, which I greatly appreciated but we were then told we'd have to wait for the night vet to come on, as they were satisfied she was triaged and was fine to wait. The night vet saw my dog after we'd waited around an hour. During this time I spoke to the lady on reception about my insurance and she said they'd make the claim and all I had to pay was my £109.00 excess and a £25.00 admin fee, which I paid whilst I was waiting.
She was clipped to facilitate cleaning and inspecting the wound and after half an hour, the Vet (Amanda) came to discuss what she'd found, which luckily was just soft tissue damage with the stick not penetrating the chest cavity.  However, she could cut everything open even more and explore the damage in precise detail if I wanted... No, that seems excessive I said. Rhetorically, she asked, is that because she's alright? A weird and unnecessary conversation which gave me the impression that she was trying to rack up as much cost as possible; a thought further confirmed when the dog was brought out wearing a 'compression' jacket that was around 4 sizes too big and incapable of compressing anything. That was another thirty minutes wait to insert 2 staples.
I was about to leave when I was presented with another bill for £457.22, which Amanda insisted I had to pay before I leave. Yes, but you've already taken £109.00 off me for the excess and this isn't reflected in the bill. Everyone has to pay the excess she said. Yes, but after paying this bill, I've now paid it twice. She insisted it was all correct and I ended up walking out having paid nearly £600 to clean and staple a superficial chest wound, including anti-biotics and anti-inflammatory. I did phone up to complain about the overcharge and they agreed that I had been overcharged and refunded my excess. All in all, I was left with a feeling that this is a practice who will happily profiteer on the back of any pet emergency you may encounter (£200 consultation fee, just because I wasn't registered there, why?). They couldn't explain why one long standing staff member understood their insurance claim procedure to be completely different to the night vets interpretation, but said they were trialling a different approach and would feed back my comments about my experience. What they don't seem to get is that many have pet insurance simply because they don't have the disposable income to shell out £600.00 over the counter for exorbitant vet fee's. They have it because they can only manage to pay their insurance excess.

Yet at this clinic, the staff ignored that confirmation, relied heavily on the old report, and insisted the swelling must be linked to leftover fragments.

The vets here fixated on that old report, dismissed infection as a possible cause, and pressured us to agree to procedures they openly admitted they could not carry out themselves. We were initially told his blood tests were “great,” but later discovered they were abnormal and did show signs of infection.
